First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264109/assets/6eb672fe024f024f20c7c3c80947d1b47bade8f998e705d6f411ae3f298ecde2.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is $\pi .$

- Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x)=-\operatorname{cot}⁡x.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\operatorname{cot}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x+3\pi ) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x+\pi \cdot 3) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the oddness of $\operatorname{cot}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x) & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\  & =-(-\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x+3\pi )=\frac{1}{8}.$
